title: Ukraine clashes with its own allies
ticker: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine - first recall since 2008
Ukraine FM Sybiha on POW row: "I consider this matter already closed"
Lee Jae-myung: Ukraine made the South Korean president a "liar"
Trump to Zelensky on refinery strikes: "He better damn well stop"

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Ukraine depends on its friends to survive this war. But lately, it keeps *clashing with them*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: South Korea has *recalled its ambassador* from Kyiv, and is demanding a public apology Ukraine *refuses to give*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Washington is furious over *refinery strikes*, and fights with *Europe*, *Poland* and even *Japan* have spilled into the open.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We start in Seoul.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It began with two North Korean soldiers.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: They were captured by Ukraine in January 2025, in Russia's *Kursk region*, where North Korea had sent troops to fight for Moscow.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Both said they wanted to live in *South Korea*. In mid-September, they arrived in Seoul.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul says both governments had agreed to keep the transfer *secret*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The reason: the soldiers' *families are still in North Korea*, where they could face reprisals.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Under South Korea's constitution, all North Koreans are considered *citizens* of the South.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And both men had already been *photographed* by South Korean media, making them easy to identify.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: Disclosed the transfer of two North Korean POWs to South Korea.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Then, in a speech to the *United Nations General Assembly*, Zelensky announced the transfer to the world.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: South Korea's spy agency told lawmakers the move appeared aimed at building support in South Korea for *sending weapons to Ukraine*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul has given Kyiv financial and humanitarian aid, but *no lethal weapons*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: South Korea has become a major *arms exporter*, with a multibillion dollar deal with Poland, but it has a long-standing policy of *not arming countries at war*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: President Lee Jae-myung called the disclosure *deeply regrettable*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The next day, a Zelensky adviser said there had been *no confidentiality agreement* at all.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv's foreign ministry later changed its tune, blaming *different interpretations* of the deal.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul's presidential office said it was *Ukraine* that had asked for secrecy in the first place.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv was worried about criticism at home for not trading the soldiers for *Ukrainian prisoners* held by Russia.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador, and demanded an *official explanation and apology*.

scenes.name: Lee Jae-myung
scenes.role: President of South Korea · on X
scenes.quote: This is a matter concerning the dignity of the Republic of Korea and its people and cannot be overlooked.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Lee then went further. He said Ukraine had made the South Korean president *a liar*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: This is a matter concerning the *dignity* of the Republic of Korea, he wrote, and cannot be overlooked.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: If Ukraine keeps refusing to publicly apologize, he warned, Seoul will take *further measures*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also criticized Zelensky's chief of staff, *Kyrylo Budanov*, who had warned that tension on the Korean border was rising by the day. Lee said it sounded *as if he were wishing for war*.

scenes.sign: EMBASSY OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On October eighth, Seoul *recalled its ambassador* to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It was South Korea's first ambassador recall since 2008, when it pulled its envoy from *Japan* over the Dokdo islets.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Park arrived back in Seoul on October tenth.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul says he may return only after Ukraine admits the secrecy deal existed, *apologizes in public*, and promises it won't happen again.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: At home, some critics in Seoul pointed out that the government moved fast against Ukraine, while being *extremely cautious* over the North Korean landmine blast that wounded its own soldiers.

scenes.name: Andrii Sybiha
scenes.quote: I consider this matter already closed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv's answer? *I consider this matter already closed*, said Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine handed over the soldiers as *a sign of goodwill*, he said, and *fulfilled all its obligations*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine follows the *Geneva Convention*, he said, and respects South Korea's constitution.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Earlier, he had called it a *diplomatic misunderstanding*, and said South Korea is an *important country* for Ukraine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv argues that revealing *that* the soldiers went to South Korea, rather than *how*, did not break any agreement.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul's foreign minister said a private message from Ukraine included words of apology, but fell *short of expectations*. Kyiv called it an expression of *regret*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And while Seoul was still waiting for an apology, a *second dispute* broke out.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine's sanctions commissioner, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, claimed fuel shipped from *South Korean ports* had helped Russia make up for refinery losses caused by Ukrainian strikes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul's presidential office *rejected* the claim the next day.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul says petroleum products are *not on its list* of controlled exports to Russia.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Seoul is not the only ally at odds with Kyiv. The biggest one is *Washington*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For weeks, President Trump has told Zelensky to *stop striking Russian oil refineries*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He blames those strikes for cutting *global diesel supplies* and pushing up prices for American farmers and truckers.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Trump said he told Zelensky directly. Don't hit refineries. And he went out and *he hit*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *He better damn well stop*, Trump said.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv says hitting Russia's oil industry is a *legitimate strategy*, because oil money pays for the war.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Days ago, Trump went around Kyiv entirely, striking a *diesel deal* with Putin and lifting sanctions on Russian fuel. Zelensky called it a *concession to Moscow*.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: With all respect to President Trump, it's up to our society, up to our people to choose one or another leader.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: When Trump said Ukraine should get *a new leader who can make a deal*, Zelensky pushed back.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: With all respect to President Trump, he said, it's *up to our people* to choose.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also rejected blame for fuel prices, saying they are rising *because of the war in the Middle East*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky says Ukraine will stop hitting refineries only if Russia stops hitting *Ukraine's power grid*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And earlier this year, a fight over oil split Ukraine from *two EU members*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In January, Russian oil stopped flowing through the *Druzhba pipeline* to Slovakia and Hungary.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine said a *Russian drone strike* had wrecked the pipeline near the Brody oil hub, making transit *physically impossible*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Slovakia's Prime Minister *Robert Fico* accused Zelensky of lying, and of blocking the oil on purpose for *political leverage*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Slovakia, which relies on a single refinery built for Russian crude, declared an *energy state of emergency*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Slovakia cut *emergency electricity* to Ukraine in the middle of winter. Slovakia and Hungary also suspended *diesel exports* to Ukraine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Hungary tied its veto on new EU sanctions against Russia to the oil flow. Kyiv told Budapest to send its complaints *to Moscow*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Oil only resumed in late April. That same day, a *90 billion euro* EU aid package for Ukraine was unblocked.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Fico welcomed the restart, but said the crisis had been used as a *geopolitical tool*, and that trust with Kyiv was *badly damaged*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Ukraine has also had *public spats* with two more key supporters: *Japan* and *Poland*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In August, Zelensky spoke to a gathering of ambassadors in Kyiv.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He singled out *Japan*. Ukraine's relations with Tokyo, he said, have *not met Kyiv's high expectations*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He noted that Japan had recently *eased its limits* on exporting lethal weapons.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: With all due respect, and we are grateful for Japan's support, but they have not been as significant as they could have been.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: With all due respect, and we are grateful for Japan's support, he said, the results *have not been as significant as they could have been*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Japan has pledged about *6 billion dollars* in humanitarian and technical aid for 2026 alone.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It also sent Ukraine a *1.3 billion dollar* grant funded by profits from frozen Russian assets.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tokyo is now weighing *stronger defense cooperation* with Kyiv.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Poland, Ukraine's closest neighbor and one of its biggest backers, had an even *bigger fight* with Kyiv.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In May, Zelensky gave a special forces unit the honorary name *Heroes of the UPA*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The UPA was a Ukrainian nationalist force. In World War Two, it carried out the *Volhynia massacres*, killing tens of thousands of Poles.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Poland officially calls the massacres *genocide*.

scenes.name: Karol Nawrocki
scenes.quote: For the overwhelming majority of Polish society, the UPA remains, above all, a formation responsible for brutal crimes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Polish President *Karol Nawrocki* responded by stripping Zelensky of Poland's highest honor, the *Order of the White Eagle*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He said Zelensky had given Russian propaganda *the best material*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Former Polish president *Lech Walesa* said the decision had insulted him and all Poles who were murdered.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky's reply? He *mailed the medal back* to Warsaw, by courier, the very next day.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He noted the same honor had once gone to *Catherine the Great*, *Mussolini* and Germany's *Gerhard Schroeder*. If Poland thinks it should stay with them, he said, Ukraine *will not argue*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Three former Ukrainian presidents returned their medals too.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Polish Prime Minister *Donald Tusk* called the row a strategic mistake that will *cost both sides*, and Brussels warned it *plays into Russia's hands*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Partner after partner, the same pattern.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In each case, Kyiv says it is acting in its *own national interest* while fighting for survival.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But one analysis in The Diplomat concluded that Kyiv has *lost the trust* of Seoul, and that the damage cannot be repaired in private.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine's foreign ministry says *diplomacy should prevail over emotions*, and that talks with Seoul continue through private channels.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: South Korea's ambassador is home, and Kyiv says the case is closed.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following whether Ukraine and its allies can *mend these rifts*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: If you found this helpful, please *like and subscribe* for more.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching.
